records.qtitle: Ratio of doctors and hospital beds
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) the details of the ratio of doctors per 1000 population currently vis-a-vis the World Health Organization (WHO) standard, State and UT-wise; <br/><br/>(b) the details of the ratio of hospital beds per 1000 population currently vis-a-vis the World Health Organization (WHO) standard; State and UT-wise; and <br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to  increase the number of doctors and hospital beds in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a):    As per information provided by Medical Council of India, there are a total 11,57,771 allopathic doctors registered with the State Medical Councils/Medical Council of India as on 31st  January, 2019. Assuming 80% availability, it is estimated that around 9.26 lakh doctors may be actually available for active service. It gives a doctor-population ratio of 1:1457 as per current population estimate of 1.35 billion, which is low as compared with the WHO norm of 1:1000. State – wise details of doctors registered with State Medical Councils / Medical Council of India is annexed at Annexure – I.<br/> Besides, there are 7.86 lakh Ayurveda, Unani and Homeopathy (AUH) doctors in the country. Assuming 80% availability, it is estimated that around 6.28 lakh Ayurveda, Unani and Homeopathy (AUH) doctors may actually available for active service and considered together with allopathic doctors, it gives a doctor population ratio of 1:868 which is better than the  standards laid down by the World Health Organization<br/>(b):     The details of number of beds in different states is not maintained centrally. However, the total number of Government hospitals and beds in these hospitals, State/UT-wise, as per National Health Profile, 2018, compiled by Central Bureau of Health Intelligence (CBHI) are 23582 and 710761, respectively. The State/UT-wise details are given at Annexure-II. <br/>(c):     Public Health and hospitals being a State subject, the primary responsibility of providing accessible, affordable and quality healthcare  to its citizens lies with the State Governments. However, in the case of Central Government Hospitals, it is informed that 500 beds in new emergency block and 807 beds  in Super Specialty Block have been added at Safdarjung Hospital. Further, the Government has taken the following steps to increase the number of doctors.<br/>For increasing UG Seats:-<br/>(i)  Enhancement of maximum intake capacity at MBBS level from 150 to 250.<br/>(ii)  Relaxation in the norms of setting up of Medical College in terms of requirement for land, faculty, staff, bed/bed strength and other infrastructure.<br/>(iii) Strengthening/ upgradation of existing State Government/Central Government   Medical Colleges to increase MBBS seats.<br/>(iv) Establishment of New Medical Colleges attached with district/referral hospitals   preferably in underserved districts of the country.<br/>For increasing PG Seats:-<br/>(i)   The ratio of teachers to students has been revised from 1:1 to 1:2 for all MD/MS disciplines and from 1:1 to 1:3 in subjects of Anesthesiology, Forensic Medicine, Radiotherapy, Medical Oncology, Surgical Oncology and Psychiatry in all medical colleges across the country. Further, teacher: student ratio in public funded Government Medical Colleges for Professor has been increased from 1:2 to 1:3 in all clinical subjects and for Asso. Prof. from 1:1 to 1:2 if the Asso. Prof. is a unit head. The same has also been extended to the private medical colleges with the conditions that it should have a standing of 15 years, running PG courses since 10 years, should have completed at least 1 continuance of recognition assessment satisfactorily and applies u/s 10A of the IMC Act, 1956 for increase of seats. This would result in increase in number of PG seats in the country.<br/>(ii)    DNB qualification has been recognized for appointment as faculty to take care of shortage of faculty.<br/> (iii)   Enhancement of age limit for appointment/ extension/ re-employment against posts of teachers/dean/principal/ director in medical colleges upto70 years.<br/> (iv)   Strengthening/ upgradation of State Government Medical Colleges for starting new PG courses/Increase of PG seats.   <br/>(v)   One time increase in PG seats was permitted in 2017-18 and again in 2018-19 in Government Medical Colleges.<br/>(vi)   By amending the regulations, it has been made mandatory for all medical colleges to start PG courses within 3 years from the date of their MBBS recognition / continuation of recognition.<br/>(vii)   Colleges are allowed to apply for PG courses in clinical subjects at the time of 4th renewal.      It will serve to advance the process for starting PG courses by more than 1 year.<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Committee to revise CSR framework
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) whether the Ministry has set up any Committee to revisit the provisions of the existing Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) rules; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof as well as the reasons therefor; <br/>(c) the recommendations suggested by the Committee; and <br/>(d) the steps taken by Government to implement the recommendations?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER FOR FINANCE<br/>AND CORPORATE AFFAIRS             (Ms. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN)<br/>(a) to (d):  The High Level Committee on CSR-2018 has been re-constituted on 22.11.2018 under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs to review the existing framework and guide and formulate the roadmap for coherent policy on CSR. The Terms of Reference of the Committee included:<br/>i.	To review the CSR framework as per Act, Rules and Circulars issued from time to time;<br/>ii.	To recommend guidelines for enforcement of CSR provisions;<br/>iii.	To suggest measures for adequate monitoring and evaluation of CSR by companies;<br/>iv.	To examine and recommend audit (financial, performance, social) for CSR, as well as, analyse outcomes of CSR activities/programmes/projects.<br/>v.	Any other matter incidental or connected thereto. <br/><br/><br/>The Committee is deliberating on the above mentioned terms of reference. <br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Lion conservation
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a)	the details of funds allocated for the conservation of lions during the last three years;<br/>(b)	the steps taken by Government for the conservation of lions in the wake of their deaths due to viral diseases; and<br/>(c)	the reasons behind Government not relocating lions from Gujarat to other States despite the Supreme Court order?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE  IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/>(SHRI BABUL SUPRIYO) <br/><br/>(a)		Ministry through its Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS)-Development of Wildlife Habitats (DWH) provides funds to the States/ UTs including the State of Gujarat for carrying various activities for conservation of Lions and their habitat. <br/><br/>The details of funds released from the CSS-DWH for the conservation of Lions during the last three years are as follows:<br/><br/>S. No.	Year	Funds released<br/>(amount in Rs. Lakh)<br/>1.	2016-17	100.09<br/>2.	2017-18	233.69<br/>3.	2018-19	280.78<br/><br/>With a view to strengthen the conservation initiatives to protect Asiatic Lion, Ministry has also approved a three year (FY:2018-19, FY:2019-20 and FY: 2020-21) dedicated project titled “Asiatic Lion Conservation Project” with a total budget of Rs. 97.85 Cr. The project envisages a scientific management prescription with involvement of communities along with coordination with multi-sectoral agencies. An amount of Rs. 17.03 Cr. is being released by the Ministry for implementation of activities during first year of the project. <br/><br/><br/>(b)		<br/>As per the information received from the State Forest Department of Gujarat, the following steps have been undertaken for the conservation of Lions in the wake of their deaths due to viral diseases:<br/><br/>1.	Veterinary hospitals are equipped with fully automatic biochemistry analyzer, Haematology Analyzer, Sonography machines, Digital C-Ray machines, Laminar.<br/>2.	Lions habitating in affected area have been vaccinated.<br/>3.	Ambulances duly equipped with modern medical equipment is put under operation.<br/>4.	Rescue Centres are equipped with vehicles, tranquilizer guns and with other rescue kits.<br/>5.	Veterinary Doctors are engaged on contractual basis. <br/><br/>Better management of Lion habitat, Disease control and veterinary care for overall conservation of Lion is also included in the dedicated three year project titled ‘Asiatic Lion Conservation project’.<br/><br/><br/>(c)	<br/>The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in I.A. No. 100 in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 337/1995 in Centre for Environment Law, WWF-I vs Union of India & Others had vide their order dated 15th April 2013 directed the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to take urgent steps for re-introduction of Asiatic lion from Gir forests to Kuno in accordance with the guidelines issued by IUCN. Hon’ble Court vide the said order had also directed the Ministry to constitute an Expert Committee for this purpose.<br/><br/>In compliance of the directions of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has constituted an Expert Committee. The committee is examining the process of translocation. The State Specific Empowered Committees have also been constituted in the State of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat under the chairmanship of their respective Chief Wild Life Wardens for overlooking the translocation process. The translocation will be done only after mutual consultations between State specific empowered committees of the two States covering all aspects of translocation including evaluation of the habitat proposed for the translocation, procedures and guidelines required to be followed for translocation and also the safety and security aspects of the translocation.<br/><br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Coal supply rationalisation scheme
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) whether coal supply rationalisation scheme has been extended to private power producers;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof as well as the reasons therefor;<br/>(c) the impact of the scheme on the consumers; and<br/>(d) the total savings accrued because of the scheme so far?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/> <br/>MINISTER OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS, COAL AND MINES <br/> <br/>(SHRI PRALHAD JOSHI)<br/> <br/>(a) & (b): Yes Sir. Ministry of Coal has issued the Policy for Linkage Rationalization for Independent Power Producers (IPPs) on 15.05.2018. The policy envisages to undertake a comprehensive review of existing sources of coal and consider the feasibility for rationalization of sources with a view to optimize the transportation cost and materialization taking into account coal availability and logistics.<br/> <br/>(c) & (d): As per request received from consumers,  linkage rationalization of eligible IPPs  has been done at Coal India Limited (CIL) for a total rationalized quantity  of 2 Million Tonnes. The annual potential savings estimated by Central Electricity Authority for the above rationalization would be about Rs. 118 crore.<br/> <br/>****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Encroachment of Defence lands
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) whether there has been an increase in cases of illegal transfer of Government land in defence estates across the country during last three years, if so, details thereof;<br/><br/><br/>(b) details of action taken against individuals / entities on the above cases during the last three years;<br/><br/>(c) measures being taken to prevent incidence of such cases in the future;<br/><br/>(d) whether Government has prepared digital database of the defence estates / land / properties in the country, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(e) total defence land under the control of Directorate General of Defence Estates till date in different States / Union Territories of the country including West Bengal?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>      DR. SUBHASH BHAMRE<br/><br/>(a)  No, Sir.<br/>(b)  In cases of illegal transfer based on the nature and circumstances of the case, FIRs / criminal cases have been filed against the sellers / purchasers, Courts have been approached to set aside such transactions.  Competent Revenue authorities have also been approached for not effecting mutation of such transactions.  Such transactions are not recognised and no mutation in defence land records are effected.<br/><br/>(c)  To prevent such incidences in future, the following steps are taken:-<br/>(i)	The defence land across the country has been surveyed by Defence Estates Officers and Chief Executive Officers so as to clearly demarcate defence land to enable Services / Users to physically protect it. <br/>(ii)	Matter has been taken up with the State Governments vigorously at all levels to mutate remaining defence land in the revenue records.<br/>(iii)	Suggestions have been made by the Ministry to the Department of Land Resources for amending the Registration Act so as to make it mandatory for the Sub-Registrar to obtain ‘NOC’ from defence authorities prior to effecting registration of land located in Cantonments / Military Stations.<br/>(iv)	Wherever such incidence is reported, immediate legal action is taken to protect the interest of Government.<br/>(v)	Computerisation of defence Land records contained in General Land Registers (GLRs) and Military Land Registers (MLRs) with the use of Raksha Bhoomi Software.<br/>(vi)	Strengthening of defence land management by way of digitisation of land records, survey, demarcation and verification of defence lands and land Audit.<br/><br/>(d)  Yes, Sir.  The computerization of defence land records under the project ‘Raksha Bhoomi’ was undertaken by the Directorate General of Defence Estates in association with National Informatics Centre.  Defence Land Records contained in General Land Registers (GLRs) and Military Land Registers (MLRs) were entered in the Raksha Bhoomi Software and made operational after verification and authentication of database in July, 2011.<br/>(e) Total defence land under the management of Defence Estates Organisation in the country is 66,103 acres.  State & Union Territories-wise details, including West Bengal are enclosed herewith as Annexure-A.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Framework for doubling farm income
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: <br/>(a) 	whether Government has created any framework for doubling farm incomes, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) 	the details of farm incomes earned by rural households in real terms in the last three years, State/UT-wise; <br/><br/>(c) 	the recommendations of the inter-ministerial committee set up to suggest ways on doubling farm incomes; and <br/><br/>(d) 	the steps taken by Government to implement these recommendations along with the impact of those measures on farm income therefrom?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>( SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)  <br/><br/>(a):	The Government has set a target of doubling of farmers’ income by the year 2022. The Government has constituted an Inter-Ministerial Committee to examine issues relating to doubling of farmers’ income and recommend a strategy to achieve doubling of farmers’ income in real terms by the year 2022. The Committee has submitted its report. <br/><br/>(b):    National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) has not conducted any survey during the last three years for collecting data of the present income of country’s farmers residing in various parts of the country. However, NSSO conducted a Situation Assessment Survey (SAS) of Agricultural households during its 70th round (January 2013- December 2013) in the rural areas of the country with reference to the agricultural year July 2012- June 2013. The survey collected the details of income generated by the agricultural households during the agricultural year July 2012-June 2013 from different economic activities. Average monthly income (Rs.) per agricultural household for different States/ group of UTs during July 2012 - June 2013 as per the results of the Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households, NSS 70th round (January 2013 – December 2013) is annexed.<br/><br/><br/>Contd….2/-<br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>Further, the Committee, which has submitted its report, containing the strategy for doubling of farmers income by the year 2022, has extrapolated the results of  the year 2012-13 survey to the year 2015-16 at 2015-16 prices and shown that average farmers income stands at Rs. 96,703/- per year. <br/><br/>(c) & (d):	The Committee has identified seven sources of income growth viz., improvement in crop productivity; improvement in livestock productivity; resource use efficiency or savings in the cost of production; increase in the cropping intensity; diversification towards high value crops; improvement in real prices received by farmers; and shift from farm to non-farm occupations. <br/><br/>            Several initiatives have already been taken among each of the above mentioned strategies which inter-alia include:<br/><br/>(i)	Initiating market reforms through the State Governments. <br/>(ii)	Encouraging contract farming through the State Governments by promulgating of Model Contract Farming Act.<br/>(iii)	Up-gradation of Gramin Haats to work as centers of aggregation and for direct purchase of agricultural commodities from the farmers.  <br/>(iv)	Launch of e-NAM initiative to provide farmers an electronic online trading platform. <br/>(v)	Implementation of flagship scheme of distribution of Soil Health Cards to farmers so that the use of fertilizers can be optimized. <br/>(vi)	“Per drop more crop” initiative under which drip/sprinkler irrigation is being encouraged for optimal utilization of water. <br/>(vii)	“Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)” under which organic farming is being promoted.  <br/>(viii)	With a view to provide better insurance coverage to crops for risk mitigation, Government has launched a crop insurance scheme namely Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) from Kharif 2016 season. This scheme provides insurance cover for all stages of the crop cycle including post-harvest risks in specified instances.<br/> (ix)	Under “Har Medh Par Ped”, agro forestry is being promoted.  With the amendment of Indian Forest Act, 1947 Bamboo grown outside forest area has been removed from the definition of trees and a mission have been launched to promote bamboo plantation. <br/><br/>Contd….3/-<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>-3-<br/>(x)	Giving a major boost for the farmers income, the Government has approved the increase in the Minimum Support Price (MSPs) for all Kharif & Rabi crops for 2018-19 season at a level of at least 150 percent of the cost of production.<br/>(xi)	Giving a major boost to the pro-farmer initiatives, the Government has approved a new Umbrella Scheme ‘Pradhan Mantri Annadata  Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA)’.  The Scheme is aimed at ensuring remunerative prices to the farmers for their produce as announced in the Union Budget for 2018. This is an unprecedented step taken by Govt. of India to protect the farmers’ income which is expected to go a long way towards the welfare of farmers.  <br/>(xii)	 Bee keeping has been promoted under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) to increase the productivity of crops through pollination and increase the honey production as an additional source of income of farmers. <br/>(xiii)	Rashtriya Gokul Mission to enhance milk production and productivity of bovines and to make milk production more remunerative to the farmers.<br/>(xiv)	National Livestock Mission to increase productivity and genetic improvement of livestock. <br/>(xv)  Foreseeing high potential in fisheries sector, a Blue Revolution with multi dimensional activities mainly focusing on fisheries production, both inland and marine is being implemented.<br/>(xvi)  The Government provides total interest subvention up to 5% (inclusive of 3% prompt repayment incentive) on short-term crop loans up to Rs. 3.00 lakh. Thus, loan is available to farmers at a reduced rate of 4% per annum on prompt repayment. <br/>(xvii) Government sets annual target for the flow of credit to the agriculture sector, Banks have been consistently surpassing the annual target. The current year’s agriculture credit flow target has been set at Rs. 11 lakh crore.<br/>(xviii)	The Government with a view to augment the income of Small and Marginal Farmers, in the Union Budget 2019 has announced “Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAmman Nidhi (PM-KiSaN)” a new Central Sector Scheme will be 100% funded by the Government of India.<br/>			Under the Scheme, financial benefit of Rs.6000/- per year will be provided to all Small and Marginal Farmer families irrespective of age and having cultivable land holding upto 2 hectare. This financial benefit will be provided in 3 equal installments of Rs.2000/- each in a period of every four months in a financial year. The benefit shall be admissible under the scheme w.e.f. 01.12.2018.<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Impact of Mid Day Meal Scheme on enrolment
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a)	the number of schools and children covered under the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (MDMS) during the last three years, State/ UT-wise; <br/><br/>(b)	the details of funds allocated and utilised under the scheme during the above period, State/UT-wise; <br/><br/>(c) whether enrolment in schools has increased after introduction of the scheme and if so, the extent of increase reported in each State/UT during the above period, gender-wise; <br/><br/>(d) whether alleged irregularities including serving of substandard meal have been reported; and <br/><br/>(e) if so, the details thereof and action taken against those responsible?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/> (SH. PRAKASH  JAVADEKAR)<br/><br/>(a)	to (e):	A statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/><br/>Statement referred to reply to parts (a) to (e) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 59 for 07.02.2019 raised by Shri Md. Nadimul Haque regarding Impact of Mid-Day Meal Scheme on enrolment.<br/><br/>(a)	to (c): The National Programme of Mid-Day Meal in Schools, popularly known as the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (MDMS), is an on-going Centrally-Sponsored Scheme which covers all school children studying in Classes I-VIII of Government, Government-Aided Schools, Special Training Centres including Madarsas and Maqtabs supported under Samagra Shiksha.  On an average basis 9.51 crore children studying in 11.34 lakh schools are served hot cooked mid-day meal on each school working day. State and UT wise details during each of the last three years are given at Annexure-I. <br/><br/>Government of India incurs per meal cost of Rs 6.64 and Rs 9.59 for students of primary and upper primary classes respectively, on an average basis. A provision of Rs 10,000 crore was made during 2017-18 for Mid-Day Meal Scheme. Over and above this, the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution made a provision of Rs. 7641 crore (approximately) for annual subsidy on account of supply of food grains by Food Corporation of India at National Food Security Act, 2013  rates @ Rs. 2 and 3 per k.g. for wheat and rice respectively against the economic cost of Rs.23.45 per k.g. for wheat and Rs.32.67 per k.g. for rice. The State and UT-wise details of the fund allocated and utilized under the Scheme during each of the last three years are given at Annexure-II. <br/><br/>The MDM Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 1995 and since then there has been a huge increase in the enrolment in schools which could be due to mid-day meal to some extent. There is a marginal decline in the enrolment in government schools over last 2 years. While no specific reason can be attributed for this, it may be presumed that the cleaning of data by States and UTs is largely responsible.<br/><br/>(d) & (e): A total number of 96 complaints on irregularities including serving of substandard meal to the children were reported from various States and Union Territories during the last three years. Respective State Governments and UT Administrations were requested to furnish Action Taken Report (ATR) in the matter. As per ATRs received from States and UTs, action such as issuing warning against the official responsible, terminating the contract of concerned NGOs/Organisations, initiating criminal proceedings and imposing penalties against the defaulting persons/organisations have been taken up by the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations.  The State and UT-wise details of complaints on irregularities including serving substandard meal to the children and action taken thereon during each of the last three years is given at Annexure-III.<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Mental health facilities in Government educational institutions
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) 	Whether there is a dearth of mental health facilities in Government schools and universities across the country; <br/>(b) 	If so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; <br/>(c) 	If not, the details of availability and recruitment of trained counsellors and the student-counsellor ratio in these institutions, school/university-wise; <br/>(d) 	The details of suicides committed by students and faculty members/teachers of schools and universities during the last three years, school/university-wise; <br/>(e) 	The funds allocated, released and utilised for mental health facilities in these institutions during that period, school/ university-wise; and<br/>(f) 	   The steps taken by Government to improve such facilities in these institutions?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF<br/>HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/><br/>   (DR. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/> (a) to (c): As education is a subject in the concurrent list of the constitution, a majority of the schools are under the control of the respective state Governments. The States and UTs are advised to frame a special strategy for guidance and counselling in schools. It is recommended to have teachers qualified on guidance and counselling services and thereby capable of conducting varied guidance and counselling programmes in schools. Moreover, the existing teachers are also trained for this purpose and Guest Lectures by prominent people in different fields are also arranged. Guidance and counselling is an essential part of in-service training programmes for teachers and Principals. Under the Integrated scheme for School Education – Samagra Shiksha launched from 2018-19, there is provision for supporting States and UTs on interventions related to Guidance and counselling in schools.<br/>Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) have norms for engaging counsellors to address the needs of mental health afflicted students.  436 educational counsellors have been engaged by KVs wherever counselling and guidance services are required. Similarly, 2 counsellors per JNV (one male and one female) have been approved. In <br/>Contd….<br/>addition, principal of JNVs are authorized to engage the services of professional counsellors / psychiatrist from a Government hospital to provide guidance and support to students identified having mental health needs. Further, short term courses are arranged for training teachers for guiding and counselling of students. The trained teachers perform as master trainers for other staff in schools. Morning PT and evening games are compulsory for all students to ensure physical and mental fitness. <br/>The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has mandated appointment of counsellors and wellness teachers on full time basis. The board also inspects schools from time to time to ensure compliance of its byelaws.  <br/>NCERT has been training personnel as counsellors to work in schools for last many years specially dealing with mental health related skills. NCERT is further augmenting efforts by training teachers to work as mentors rather than only subject experts. The National Curriculum Framework (NCF), 2005 recommends measures like making examinations more flexible, provision of guidance and counselling in schools, and making learning child-centric etc. The States and UTs have adopted or adapted the NCF as per their local context. <br/>	The University Grant Commission (UGC) has framed guidelines on safety of students on or off campus of Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs). As per these guidelines HEIs should mandatorily put in place a broad base “Students counselling system” for the effective management of problems and challenges faced by the students such as anxiety, stress, etc. <br/>(d): Data on student suicides in school and college campuses is not maintained by this Ministry. However, as per the data available on ‘Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India 2015’ published by National Crime Records bureau (NCRB), a total of 8934 students had committed suicide in the year 2015. The report mentions that 1360 persons below the age of 18 years and 1183 persons below the age of 30 years committed suicide during 2015 due to failure in examination. <br/> (e) & (f): In the year 2018-19, the Department of School Education & Literacy, MHRD launched Samagra Shiksha – an integrated scheme for School Education covering children from classes I to XII which subsumes the erstwhile Centrally Sponsored Schemes of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) & Teacher Education (TE). The scheme has provisions for equitable and quality education for students from Class I to XII through dedicated components of equity and quality education. The main objective of the Samagra Shiksha Scheme is to impart quality education that facilitates the holistic development of the child. Under Samagra Shiksha, projects on guidance and counselling of students have been approved and an amount of Rs. 728.86 lakh has been approved for the year 2018-19 for this purpose. <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Development cooperation with foreign countries
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a)	the details regarding any policy document and guidelines for India''s development cooperation with foreign countries; and<br/><br/>(b)	the details of initiatives taken by Government for furthering developmental cooperation during the last three years, country-wise;<br/><br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>[GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)]<br/><br/>(a)	Development cooperation is a key instrument in India''s foreign policy. The scope and reach of India’s development cooperation has seen considerable expansion in the past few years. Developmental cooperation with the partner countries is mainly being executed through instruments such as Grant assistance, Lines of Credit and Concessional Financing Scheme. <br/><br/>One of the main instruments of India’s development cooperation include Lines of Credit (LOCs). GoI LOCs are governed by a set of guidelines jointly developed by the Ministry of External Affairs and the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) in the Ministry of Finance. These are the the guidelines under the Indian Development and Economic Assistance Scheme (IDEAS) and the latest version of the guidelines was issued on 07 December 2015. These guidelines may be accessed from the website of DEA. Grant assistance initiatives are undertaken in compliance with the General Financial Rules (GFR) of GoI and CVC Guidelines issued from time to time. Concessional Financing Scheme is governed by the ‘Guidelines on Concessional Financing Scheme (CFS) to support Indian Entities bidding for strategically important infrastructure projects abroad’ as revised in August 2018. These guidelines also are available on the website of DEA. <br/><br/>(b)	The focus of development cooperation has been the countries in India’s neighbourhood and in Africa, though India is also expanding its development cooperation reach to South East Asia, East and Central Asia, the Caribbean, Latin America, Pacific Island Countries, etc. <br/><br/>With a view to enhance our engagement with African countries, various development partnership initiatives were undertaken in the last decade, especially after India-Africa Forum Summit (IAFS) III in 2015. India announced LOCs of US$10 billion for development projects at IAFS-III in 2015 to be spread over 5 years. Projects for developing infrastructure, public transport, clean energy, irrigation, agriculture and manufacturing capacity have been envisaged to be taken up under these LOCs. Projects are under various stages of implementation under 32 LOCs extended to African countries after IAFS-III in 2015. <br/><br/>In the year 2015, guidelines governing GoI LOCs were revised with a view to improve efficiency and make the system robust and transparent. The rate of interest and tenor offered to developing countries has also been made more attractive. There has been marked improvement in the formulation and execution of projects since the new guidelines have come into effect.<br/><br/>Government has undertaken close consultations with the solar industry to ascertain sectors/projects where we have expertise. Close consultations have been held with the member countries of the International Solar Alliance (ISA), Indian Missions abroad and Missions of foreign countries in India. As a result of these sustained efforts, a total of 27 specific projects in 15 countries have been identified for implementation with an estimated  funding of US$ 1,392.48 million under GoI LOCs.  These project were announced at the ISA Summit held in New Delhi on 11 March 2018.<br/><br/>In the year 2018, Project Preparation Facility (PPF) was set up to assist partner countries in coming up with viable projects that can be considered under LOCs since many countries need support in identifying, conceiving and preparing a proper project proposal. PPF provides a quick access and demand driven mechanism in this context. Expenditure for preparing the reports for project proposed under PPF are covered by the Government. <br/><br/>*****

The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is the flagship scheme of the Ministry providing short term training to the youth through affiliated training partners/ training centres. After successful implementation of the Scheme in 2015-16, the scheme was re-launched in October, 2016 and it as PMKVY-2.0 (2016-20). The scheme is being implemented through both center and state under the two components called Centrally Sponsored Centrally Managed & Centrally Sponsored State Managed. The training is provided through three components as Short Term Training (STT), Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Special Projects.  All of PMKVY courses are NSQF aligned and has dedicated hours of training to impart digital and financial literacy in addition to core curriculum. records.qtitle: Guidelines for Online Travel Aggregators
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has prepared any guidelines on accreditation and classification of Online Travel Aggregators (OTAs); <br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof; <br/>(c) 	the details of criterion set by Government for OTAs to get approval and accreditation; <br/>(d) 	whether other establishments apart from OTAs are also bound by these guidelines and processes, if so, the details thereof; and <br/>(e) 	the details of action that can be taken if OTAs are in violation of the above guidelines?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR TOURISM (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>(SHRI K. J. ALPHONS)<br/><br/>(a) to (d):	The guidelines for the scheme of approval/re-approval of Online Travel Aggregators (OTAs) have been formulated and notified by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India. These guidelines are available in the public domain and have been published on the official website of the Ministry of Tourism. The scheme is purely voluntary in nature and it is not binding upon any Online Travel Aggregators to obtain accreditation from the Ministry of Tourism. <br/><br/>(e):	The above guidelines stipulate that if at any stage it is found that the OTA has not obtained any clearance from the local Authorities (Panchayat or Municipal) and/or State Government/Union Territory Administration and/or Government of India or it is found that such clearance (s) has /have been obtained on the basis of misrepresentation of fact (s) or if it is found that any fact mentioned in the application seeking the approval/re-approval is incorrect, then the approval/ re-approval granted by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India shall stand withdrawn with immediate effect and Director/Owner/Partner/Chairman/Managing Director/CEO and Authorized representative of the OTA shall be liable for facing criminal proceedings for misrepresentation of facts to the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India.<br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Multi Sectoral Development Programme
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) whether there has been a low achievement in physical outcomes across components under the Multi Sectoral Development Programme during last three years, if so, the reasons therefor;<br/>(b) the details of the completion rate of the sector-based infrastructure against the units sanctioned under MSDP during the last three years, State/UT-wise;<br/>(c) the details of the funds spent under the Multi Sectoral DevelopmentProgramme during the last three years, State/UT-wise;<br/>(d) the criteria used for identifying the minority concentration areas; and<br/>(e) the details of the data of the minority population living below the poverty line?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF MINORITY AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI MUKHTAR ABBAS NAQVI)<br/><br/>(a) to(c) :The Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP) has since been restructuredas Pradhan Mantri Jan VikasKaryakram (PMJVK)for its implementation during the remaining period of the 14th Finance Commission.  The scheme is demand driven and projects are sanctioned based on the felt need and requirement of the States/UTs.  The projects sanctioned under theprogramme are primarily related to construction of infrastructure viz., School/College Buildings, Hostel Buildings, Health Centres, ITIs, SadbhavMandaps, Residential Schools, Polytechnics etc.  These projects being construction projects, their pace of construction depend upon various factors including availability of land, award of work contract through tenders, timely release of funds by the States to implementing agencies etc. In general, States/UTs take 3 to 4 years to complete construction of bigger projects.  The Ministry during 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 has sanctioned around 16567, 13574 and 7604 units of various major projects and as per reports received from the States/UTs, these projects are at various stages of construction. The State/UT-wise details of the units sanctioned and funds released by the Ministry under MsDP/PMJVK during the 2015-16 to 2017-18is at Annexure-I.<br/>(d)	The Government has identified Minority Concentration Areas (MCAs) based on the criteria of substantial population of minority communities and relative backwardness in terms of identified parameters as compared to national average as per indicators of Census, 2011.  Details are available at http://www.minorityaffairs.gov.in/sites/default/files/Guidelines-PMJVK%20-latest_0.pdf.<br/><br/>(e)NITI Aayog has apprised that there is no separate poverty assessment carried out for minorities in the past. However, the Sachar Committee, in its report submitted to the Government in the year 2006, has indicated, inter alia, that in the year 2004-05, 38.4% of Muslims in urban areas and 26.9% in rural areas were below the poverty level, which is higher than the other minorities. <br/><br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: National Policy for Treatment of Rare Diseases
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether Government is facing issues of fund shortage for the implementation of policy of treatment of rare diseases;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof as well as the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(c) the salient features and guidelines of the National Policy for Treatment of Rare Diseases;<br/><br/>(d) the definition and the coverage of rare diseases under the said policy by Government; and<br/><br/>(e) the details of patients treated, funds allocated, released and utilised under the policy so far, State/UT-wise, year-wise and disease-wise?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) to (e):  	The National Policy for Treatment of Rare Diseases was formulated in the year 2017.  The said National Policy has been kept in abeyance vide non statutory Gazette Notification dated 18.12.2018 for its revision, further improvement and effective implementation till the revised Policy is issued by the Central Government or until further orders, whichever is earlier.  No funds were released to any States for treatment of rare diseases as per the erstwhile National Policy for Treatment of Rare Diseases.<br/>

records.qtitle: Detection of Suspect Account Holders
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) the details of the Suspect Account Holders detected due to the enormity of money being deposited in their accounts during demonetisation; <br/>(b) the details of the action taken by the Government against these account holders so far; <br/>(c) the details on the quantum of black money detected in these accounts as a result of the above action taken; and <br/>(d) the money collected under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana (PMGKY) so far?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI SHIV PRATAP SHUKLA)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): During demonetisation, large cash was deposited in bank accounts, and it became possible to track the owner of cash. The Income Tax Department (ITD) took prompt action on those found to be involved in misuse of the scheme of demonetisation. The cash deposit data was analyzed to identify those persons whose cash transactions did not appear to be in line with their profile. In the first phase preliminary analysis resulted in identification of about Rs. 17.92 lakh persons for verification. Regular emails and SMS were sent to them for submitting their response online. This exercise promoted voluntary compliance. <br/>        More than 1.5 lakh cases have been selected for scrutiny though Computer Assisted Scrutiny Selection for F.Y. 2017-18 and 2018-19 and relevant notices issued to them.<br/>       All these steps have resulted in an increase of Income tax return filer base by 1.07 crore new-filers and a growth rate of 18% in tax collections, in F.Y. 2017-18.<br/>        Also, during the period from November 2016 to March 2017, the Income-tax Department (ITD) conducted search and seizure actions on around 900 groups, wherein, assets worth over Rs. 900 crores were seized and undisclosed income of over Rs. 7,900 crores was admitted.<br/><br/>(d): Under the PMGKY Scheme, as per the applicable rates, the amount of taxes, surcharge and penalty paid by the declarants on the basis of declarations filed was over Rs. 2300 crores.<br/><br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Detection of Bogus Refund Claims
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether there has been an increase in the detection of Bogus Refund Claims based 		on fraudulent investments and fraudulent high-pitched assessments in the last three 		years; <br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof, State/UT and year-wise; <br/>(c)	the details of action taken against individuals and entities for the above offences in the 		last three years, State/UT-wise; <br/>(d) 	the impact of the bogus refund claims on the exchequer; and <br/>(e) 	the steps taken by Government to curb these malpractices and its impact thereon?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI SHIV PRATAP SHUKLA)<br/><br/>(a)&(b) Yes sir. There has been an increase in detection of suspicious refund claims. The 		details of number of cases selected for scrutiny to examine such claims for three years 		by Income Tax Department are as follows:<br/><br/>			FY 2018-19:     20,874<br/>			FY 2017-18:     11,059<br/>			FY 2016-17:      9,856<br/><br/>		Region-wise/ tax-jurisdiction-wise details of such cases are given in Annexure-A.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>(c)	Scrutiny assessments have been initiated against taxpayers claiming high refunds 		inconsistent with the pattern of income and investments. Wherever after scrutiny the 		claim of refund was found to be inadmissible, the same was denied and consequential 		action of penalty and prosecution was taken based on the merits of the case. In a 		number of cases, the returns already accepted by the Department have been<br/>           re-opened to re-examine the claim of refund based on local intelligence as well as 		surveys and searches conducted by the local field units.<br/><br/>(d)	Since the assessments and re-assessments of cases involving high-risk refunds are 		being undertaken by various field officers and the exercise is an on-going process, it 		is not feasible to ascertain the revenue impact of such claims.<br/><br/>(e)	As submitted above, higher number of cases involving high-risk refunds are being 		selected for scrutiny by the Income Tax Department.  The Department has also<br/> 	incorporated certain risk parameters in its System which prevents refunds from being 		automatically cleared in cases where suspicious refund claims are made in Income 		Tax Returns, especially those returns which have been filed from a single IP address 		or from a single locality or by a single intermediary. Such cases are then examined for 		possible selection in scrutiny or for electronic verification from the taxpayer. Swift<br/> 	action is taken by the Department against persons found to be involved in any<br/> 	malpractices related to refunds. <br/><br/>		In addition, the field officers have been sensitized about the increasing trend of high-		risk refunds and directed to take all necessary precautions and conduct necessary due 		diligence before admitting a claim of high refund. All refunds are being processed 		online and issued through the Refund Banker to avoid any omission or commission by 		the field officers. <br/><br/>********<br/><br/> <br/><br/>Annexure-A<br/>Scrutiny cases related to high refund-claims<br/><br/>REGIONS/ JURISDICTIONS	FY 2016-17<br/>	FY 2017-18<br/>	FY 2018-19<br/><br/>ANDHRA PRADESH AND TELENGANA	430	375	1,117<br/>BIHAR AND JHARKHAND	96	99	289<br/>DELHI	1,008	1,029	1,850<br/>GUJARAT	739	487	1,268<br/>KARNATAKA AND GOA	456	656	1,520<br/>KERALA	260	164	310<br/>MADHYA PRADESH AND CHATTISGARH	241	189	576<br/>MUMBAI	1,568	1,585	3,009<br/>NAGPUR	101	99	242<br/>NORTH EAST REGION	123	85	244<br/>NORTH WEST REGION	545	579	1,584<br/>ODISHA	89	75	220<br/>PUNE	409	510	1,097<br/>RAJASTHAN	244	183	503<br/>TAMIL NADU	657	618	1,344<br/>UTTAR PRADESH (EAST)	212	131	472<br/>UTTAR PRADESH (WEST)	229	245	532<br/>WEST BENGAL AND SIKKIM	382	306	883<br/>PCCIT INTL.TAX, DELHI	717	992	1,422<br/>CENTRAL CHARGES	574	589	1,204<br/>EXEMPTION CHARGES	776	2,063	1,188<br/>TOTAL 	9,856	11,059	20,874<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Methods used for tiger estimation
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a)	the details of the methods used for tiger estimation;<br/>(b)	whether Government has taken note of other such methods used worldwide for tiger estimation;<br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>(d)	the impact of the usage of M-STRIPES application for Tiger estimation; and <br/>(e)	the details of allocation made for the purpose of tiger estimation?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a)	The All India Tiger Estimation, 2014 was a refinement over the 2006 and 2010 exercise, wherein robust spatially explicit capture recapture protocols using joint models have been employed.  The method is peer reviewed in both national and international fora and has been published in an international scientific journal.  The national assessment 2018 is being conducted by the National Tiger Conservation Authority in collaboration with the State Forest Departments, Wildlife Institute of India and National level Non Governmental Organisations, using the same methodology.<br/><br/>(b) & (c)Peer reviewed literature and processes have been consulted and fine tuned to India’s field requirement.  Tiger population estimation in India is based on published standard methodology which is thoroughly grounded in field craft and adapted to Indian conditions.<br/><br/>(d)M-STrIPES (Monitoring system for Tigers’ Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) has resulted in cleaner data receipt from the field for processing and analysis.<br/><br/>(e)An amount of Rs. 1022.21 lakhs has been sanctioned to the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun for the All India Tiger Estimation, while an amount of Rs. 809.02 lakhs has been sanctioned to the States under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Project Tiger for the purpose of tiger estimation.<br/><br/>***<br/><br/>

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER FOR SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND<br/>MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES<br/>(DR. HARSH VARDHAN)<br/><br/>(a)	and (b)	Yes. Government has recently conducted Seismic Microzonation in Delhi and Kolkata and released the reports in February 2016. Copies of these reports have also been given to stakeholders of concerned State and Central Governments. Seismic Microzonation of some other parts like Sikkim, Guwahati, Bengaluru etc. has been also conducted in project mode.<br/><br/>(c)	National Centre for Seismology (NCS), Ministry of Earth Sciences has proposal to carry out Seismic Microzonation of 30 more cities in the country which include Asansol District of West Bengal. Kolkata from West Bengal is already been covered for Seismic Microzonation.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>(d) 	In the first phase four cities Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Coimbatore and Mangalore have been taken up for microzonation.  Expression of Interest was invited for the second phase for eight cities (Patna, Meerut, Amritsar, Agra, Varanasi, Lucknow, Kanpur and Dhanbad) from potential Academic and Research organizations / Institutes in India” namely IIT-Patna; IIT Kanpur; IIT (ISM)-Dhanbad; IIT-Hyderabad; IIT-Delhi; IIT-Kharagpur; IIT Roorkee; IIT-Guwahati; National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI)-Hydrabad; Institute of Seismological Research (ISR)-Gandhinagar; Geophysics Division-BHU; IISc-Bangalore, and other institutes of Govt. of India/States of repute having credentials of doing the similar works.<br/><br/>(e)	In the first phase Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Coimbatore and Mangalore are being covered by two qualified bidders (M/s Fugro and M/s Secon). Second phase tendering process has been initiated on 20th December, 2018.<br/><br/>(f)	As mentioned above Government has allocated to carry out Seismic Microzonation for Delhi and Kolkata. During last three years the reports and manual of Seismic Microzonation are published on MoES website. The Project “Seismic Microzonation of 30-Cities in India” has been initiated. The budget allocated for the project “Seismic Microzonation of 30-Cities in India” is Rs. 90 crore (Ninety crore only) in last three years.<br/>

records.qtitle: Promoting Intellectual Property Rights in Defence
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has taken any measures to promote self-reliance in Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) in Defence;<br/><br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(c) the impact of such measures on cost savings; and<br/><br/>(d) the challenges faced by the Defence sector in attracting private and public sector entities for IPRs?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>DR. SUBHASH BHAMRE<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Several Ordnance Factories and Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) have been carrying out innovative research on the development of certain materials, components / sub-assemblies / assemblies leading to performance upgradation of the existing system / platforms. A need was felt to create a structured mechanism to facilitate and encourage innovative activities with a primary objective to “Boost Intellectual Property culture” which would enhance the Intellectual Capital that is vital for encouraging in-house Research & Development in such organizations. With this objective in view, an Intellectual Property Rights Facilitation (IPF) Cell has been established under the Department of Defence Production on 4th April, 2018 to promote self-reliance in Intellectual Property Rights in Defence Sector.<br/><br/>As part of this initiative, Department of Defence Production has launched the “Mission Raksha Gyan Shakti” on 27th November, 2018 to encourage Defence Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Ordnance Factory Board to boost “IPR culture” in their respective organization to promote self-reliance in defence sector. During the period July to December 2018, 304 IPRs have been filed and 8838 personnel have been trained for this purpose.<br/><br/>(c) The innovative research undertaken by Defence Public Sector Undertakings and Ordnance Factory Board is helping in indigenization of existing system / platform to bring down import contents thereby resulting in cost savings.<br/>(d) The challenges faced by the Defence Public Sector Undertakings and Ordnance Factory Board in pursuing Intellectual Property Rights in defence sector include lack of awareness and availability of trained manpower besides the need to collectively appraise the challenges ahead with private sector, Micro, Small & Medium  Enterprises (MSMEs) and end users. The Intellectual Property Rights Facilitation Cell and Mission Raksha Gyan Shakti have been created to address such challenges being faced by Defence Public Sector Undertakings and Ordnance Factory Board.<br/>******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Guidelines for clinical trials
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Government has devised guidelines for clinical trials by pharmaceutical companies; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) the details of the total number of cases resulting in deaths or permanent disabilities of patients due to clinical trials in the last three years, year-wise; <br/><br/>(d) the details of the compensation paid by Government and pharmaceutical companies for cases of deaths and permanent disabilities due to clinical trials in the last three years, year-wise; and <br/><br/>(e) the details of clinical trial sites, IECs (Institutional Ethics Committees) and principal investigators being accredited in the last three years?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) & (b):   Clinical trials of new drugs are regulated under Rules 122 DA, 122DAB, 122DAC, 122DD, 122E and Schedule-Y of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945. The detailed requirements and guidelines for permission to conduct clinical trials are specified in Schedule Y of Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945.<br/>         Draft New Drugs & Clinical Trials Rules, 2018 were published on 01-02-2018 for inviting public/stakeholder comments.<br/>(c) & (d):   Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) of death/injuries/disabilities in clinical trials may occur due to various reasons like life threatening disease, cancer, cardiovascular diseases, side effects of the investigational products etc. Such SAEs may or may not be related to clinical trials. The number of Serious Adverse Events (SAEs) of deaths, clinical trials related deaths & compensation paid   since 2016 is enclosed as annexure-I and in respect of permanent disabilities is as annexure-II.<br/>Contd……..<br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>(e):   There is no provision under Rule 122DD of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945 for accreditation of clinical trial sites, IECs (Institutional Ethics Committees) and Principal Investigator. <br/>However, there are provisions for registration of Ethics Committee. As per Rule 122DD, no Ethics Committee shall review and accord its approval to a clinical trial protocol without prior registration with Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).<br/>           Detailed guidelines and requirements for registration of Ethics Committee are specified in Rule 122DD & Appendix-VIII of Schedule Y of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules, 1945. The number of Ethics Committees registered under the said Rules during the year 2016, 2017 & 2018 are 136, 578 & 345 respectively.<br/>………………..<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Detection of undeclared foreign assets
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) the details of illicit and undeclared foreign assets detected under the Black Money Act; <br/>(b) the details of prosecution complaints filed under the Black Money Act during the last two years regarding the above; <br/>(c) the details of asset holders asked to bring back black money from abroad through the payment of a penal tax; and <br/>(d) the details of the asset holders who failed to do so and are being prosecuted under the Black Money Act during the last two years?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI SHIV PRATAP SHUKLA)<br/><br/>(a) to (d):  As an outcome of the actions taken by the Income-tax Department under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015’ (The Black Money Act), as on 31/10/2018, undisclosed foreign assets and income valued at over Rs. 6000 crores (subject to fluctuations in currency conversion) have been detected. <br/>Further, as on 31/10/2018, 34 prosecution complaints have been filed under the Black Money Act.<br/>Under the Black Money Act, a one-time compliance opportunity for a limited period was provided to those persons who have any foreign assets which have hitherto not been disclosed for the purposes of Income-tax. In this compliance window, which closed on 30th September 2015, 648 declarations involving undisclosed foreign assets worth over Rs.4100 crore were made. An amount of over Rs.2470 crore has been collected by way of tax and penalty in such cases.<br/>Suitable action against the persons who have undisclosed foreign assets and income is taken under the Black Money Act.  Such actions include enquiries, assessment of income, levy of taxes, penalties and filing of prosecution complaints in criminal courts, wherever applicable.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Geotagging of rural eevelopment works
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has started using geotagging as an audit technique for rural development works, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b)	the details of the collaboration in this regard;<br/> <br/>(c)	the details of schemes where geotagging is being used; <br/><br/>(d)	whether the local bodies have a role to play in this audit, if so, the details thereof, if not, the reasons therefor;<br/> <br/>(e)	the benefits of geotagging as compared to other auditing techniques; and<br/> <br/>(f)	the details of the funds allocated and utilised for this purpose so far?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI NARENDRA SINGH TOMAR)<br/><br/>(a) to (f):	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/>******<br/> <br/><br/>Statement in reply to Parts (a) to (f) of Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 263 for 07.01.2019<br/><br/>(a) to (d):	A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) has been signed between the Ministry of Rural Development and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Department of Space for geo-tagging the assets in each Gram Panchayat under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS). The MoU addresses specific components of geo-tagging of assets and creation of data base for online recording and monitoring. The information related to geotagged assets is available in public domain on Bhuvan Portal of National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Hyderabad. To further strengthen transparency and accountability, the Ministry has developed a Citizen Centric Mobile Application (JANMANREGA) to view and provide feedback on the geotagged assets. <br/><br/>	Under the Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), the construction of the house is monitored by capturing geo-tagged, date and time stamped photographs of pre-determined stages of construction of the house. The physical progress of stage-wise construction of houses on ground is verified and monitored using mobile based application – “AwaasApp” on AwaasSoft platform. <br/><br/>	Under Pradhan Mantri Gramin Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), the Ministry is using the services of the NRSC, Hyderabad and Centre for Geo-Informatics Application in Rural Development (CGARD), National Institute of Rural Development & Panchayati Raj (NIRD-PR) in monitoring construction of roads by using satellite imageries. As a requirement for this project, the geo tagging of the PMGSY roads is carried out using geo-pmgsy mobile application. The project is being implemented by NRSC and CGARD.<br/><br/><br/> (e):	The benefits of geotagging as compared to other auditing techniques are given below:<br/><br/>•	Geo-tagging helps in greater transparency and higher visibility to the programme<br/><br/>•	Facilitated coordination for joint use of created assets under convergence among multiple departments.<br/><br/>•	Prevents double counting of assets.<br/><br/>(f):	The Ministry has released Rs.3.35 crore to NRSC, Hyderabad for strengthening infrastructure for geotagging under MGNREGA.<br/><br/>	Under PMGSY, an amount of Rs.22.09 crore has been sanctioned for the project and an amount of Rs.6.62 crore has been released, so far, by the Ministry.<br/><br/><br/>                                                                                                                                                                                                 <br/>.<br/>

records.qtitle: Status of National Rural Drinking Water Programme
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP) has missed its targets in providing access to potable piped water and drinking water for the rural population;<br/> (b)	if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor, State/UT-wise;<br/> (c) 	the details of the performance of the programme in providing water connections to households vis-a-vis the year-wise targets during the last three years, State/ UT-wise; and<br/> (d) 	the funds allocated, released and utilised by Government for the programme during the said period?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR DRINKING WATER AND SANITATION<br/>(SHRI RAMESH CHANDAPPA JIGAJINAGI)<br/><br/>(a)& (b) Under centrally sponsored National Rural Drinking Water Programme (NRDWP), this Ministry provides technical and financial assistance to States for improving coverage of safe drinking water in rural areas. Coverage of safe drinking water in rural areas is maintained in terms of Fully Covered habitations (i.e. getting more than 40 litre per capita per day (lpcd) safe drinking water), Partially Covered habitations (i.e. getting less than 40 lpcd safe drinking water) and Quality Affected habitations (i.e. containing chemical contaminant). As reported by States on Integrated Management Information System (IMIS) of the Ministry, status of Fully Covered, Partially Covered and Quality Affected habitations is as under:<br/><br/>Coverage of habitations as on 01.04.14 (in %)	Coverage of habitations as on 03.01.19 (in %)<br/>Fully Covered	Partially Covered	Quality Affected	Fully Covered	Partially Covered	Quality Affected<br/>73.66	21.71	4.63	80.42	16.00	3.58<br/><br/>It is evident from above table that Fully Covered habitations increased by 6.76%, Partially covered habitations reduced by 5.71% and Quality Affected habitations reduced by 1.05%. It shows significant improvement in the coverage.<br/><br/>State-wise details of coverage of Fully covered, Partially Covered and Quality Affected habitations is at Annexure-I and details of percentage of population having access to piped water supply is at Annexure-II.<br/>	<br/>(c) Rural drinking water supply being a state subject, it is for the state to plan, design, implement and execute drinking water supply schemes including household connections in rural areas. As reported by States on IMIS, 17.93% of rural households have tap connection as on 03.01.2019. State-UT wise details of number of household connections for the last three years are at Annexure-III.  In Piped Water Supply Schemes, taking water connections is at the volition of the household.<br/><br/>(d) The state-wise details of fund allocated, released and utilized (expenditure) for the last three years is at Annexure-IV.<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: My Stamp scheme
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) 	the details of the postage stamps printed under My Stamp scheme so far; <br/><br/>(b) 	the details of the revenue earned through these postage stamps under the scheme so far, State/UT-wise; <br/><br/>(c) 	whether Government has received cases of misuse of the My Stamp scheme by individuals/entities so far, if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(d) 	the details of action taken against the above; and <br/><br/>(e) 	the measures taken by Government to prevent misuse of the My Stamp scheme?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS &<br/> MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/>(SHRI MANOJ SINHA)<br/><br/>(a)	“MY STAMP” is the brand name for personalized sheets of Postage Stamps of Department of Posts. The personalization is achieved by printing a thumb nail photograph of the customer images and logos of institutions, or images of artwork, heritage buildings, famous tourist places, historical cities, wildlife, other animals and birds etc., alongside the selected My Stamp theme stamp.<br/><br/>“CUSTOMIZED MY STAMP” is a personalized sheet of Postage Stamps wherein the corporate, organizations and institutions can get their customized sheets printed from Department of Posts. records.qtitle: Standard Operating Procedures for cleaning of sewers and septic tanks
records.name: Mohammed Nadimul Haque
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has released the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for cleaning of sewers and septic tanks for field staff; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c) whether the procedures are legally enforceable and if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(e) the details of technological interventions brought or introduced by Government for cleaning of sewers and septic tanks?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/>(SHRI THAAWAR CHAND GEHLOT)<br/><br/>(a)  to (e): A statement is laid on the Table of the House. <br/><br/> <br/>Statement referred in reply to part (a) to (e) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question No.237 for answer on 03.01.2019 raised by Shri Md. Nadimul Haque regarding “Standard operating procedure for cleaning of sewers and septic tanks”.<br/><br/><br/>(a) and (b): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs which is the administrative Ministry for these issues has informed that the urban sanitation is a State subject and the State Government is responsible to plan, design, execute and operate sanitation schemes in urban areas of the country.  Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has released Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for cleaning of sewers and septic tanks on 19.11.2018, which prescribes the procedure for cleaning, its frequency, equipment needed, protective and safety gear to be used, emergency preparedness, procedures to be followed for emergency during inspection and cleaning and also the roles and responsibility of various stakeholders. SOP is a voluminous document and is available in the public domain at http://amrut.gov.in/writereaddata/amrut_SOP.pdf.<br/><br/>(c) and (d): Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has further informed that SOP is advisory in nature to guide the States/Union Territories (UTs) and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in the process of cleaning sewers and emptying septic tanks in scientific ways.<br/><br/>Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has also released Manual of Sewerage and Sewage Treatment Systems, 2013 in which detailed description of various  methods of cleaning of sewers and septic tanks are available. This Manual is available in the public domain at http://mohua.gov.in/publication/latest-manual-on-sewerage-and-sewage-treatment-systems-2013.php<br/><br/>*****<br/>
